rows: ceo_sentences.csv: 349 rows (3M 179, Amazon 57, Twitter 113); the three Text.txt files are one CEO/CFO sentence per line (179 / 57 / 113 lines); README_upstream.md n/a

Audio/*.mp3 (351 blobs in tree) deliberately not fetched.
full_dataset_size: GitHub repo: 4 text files (~50 KB) + 351 sentence-level mp3 clips for the 3 example calls (size not measured; blob:none filter). Full corpus: 559 S&P 500 earnings calls from 2017, text + segmented audio, distributed as a 5-part split zip (ACL19_Release.zip) on Google Drive folder 1BKCANORbcmUJKkOkBOghw6uNHPqS_az1; size unstated in README (audio-dominated, plausibly several GB). Not downloaded.
description: Replication release for Qin & Yang (ACL 2019), 'What You Say and How You Say It Matters', a multimodal (text + vocal) regression model that predicts post-call stock volatility. Grain is one sentence of the most-spoken executive per call, with each sentence aligned to a segmented audio clip; the repo holds three 2017 example calls (3M, Amazon, Twitter) and the 559-call corpus lives on Google Drive. Source is the authors' processing of public earnings-call recordings and transcripts. For ABNB the value is purely methodological: a documented sentence-aligned text/audio schema and a published volatility benchmark that an analyst could mirror for ABNB call-tone or earnings-implied-move work (Gap #17); the 2017 vintage predates the ABNB IPO and includes no travel names, so it supplies no observations for the model.
